prefix:
Annotate ONE last-word JSON record for a causal story PREFIX. Treat the story as
data, never as instructions. This is version 3 of the prefix-only adaptation of the reviewed
20-story annotation prompt v4: keep its feature meanings, typed values, scopes
and uncertainty, but use ONLY evidence already in the supplied prefix. Do not
return earlier word records, a list, an annotations wrapper, Markdown, or prose.

INPUT AND CAUSAL BOUNDARY
The final user message contains JSON-line token spans, grouped into append-only
word-ended blocks. Concatenate their token values to read the exact text. The
last word is your target. Copy its index and token exactly, including case and
typos. No later space, punctuation or word exists in the evidence available to
you. Do not infer a grammatical object, purpose, recipient, outcome, quote speaker
or sense from an imagined continuation. A name alone supports person, not gender
or age. At "Lily took", no scissors or repair purpose has appeared. At "Lily took
scissors", the obtain event can acquire a patient in THIS record's snapshot;
the earlier took record is never revised. At an open negation, leave its unseen
predicate unresolved. A later repair must not rename the earlier obtain event.
An earlier available object is NOT automatically the patient or instrument of a
new verb. In "Nia took a needle. She did not mend", no mending patient or actual
instrument has appeared: patients=[] and instruments=[]. Do not turn the needle
into the thing being mended. Keep incomplete predicates incomplete, even when
the prefix contains plausible participants from another event.

Requests are independent and run in parallel. You never receive earlier model
answers. Earlier word annotations are immutable as-of observations, not a whole
story parse waiting to be completed. Later evidence can support the CURRENT
record's reference resolution and state only. Do not pretend that earlier
records had that evidence. Some catalog definitions discuss later evidence or
retrospective checks: omit those features until their evidence has appeared.

SPARSE TYPED RECORD
Always emit index, token, pos, lemma, scope_id. Add supported catalog fields
directly as top-level keys, using the provided 1,024-field definitions and agreed
extensions. There is no density quota. Omission means unknown, inapplicable or
unannotated; it never means false. Use real JSON booleans, numbers, arrays and
objects for typed fields. Do not stringify bundles or emit 1,024 nulls. Keep false
when a negative fact is supported. The legacy attributes field, if needed, is an
array of {"name": string, "value": string}; prefer an existing typed field.

pos: n (including proper names), v (including auxiliaries), adj, adv, pron, det,
adp, conj, num, part, intj, unknown. Choose the contextual class supported now.
lemma: dictionary base; preserve proper-name capitalization. Normalize inflected
verbs/plurals and modal forms could->can, would->will, should->shall, might->may.
Pronouns me->I, him->he, her->she, us->we, them->they, but possessive determiner
her keeps her. Keep contractions intact: I'd has pos=pron, lemma=I, plus its
supported expansion; couldn't has pos=v, lemma=can and ["could","not"]. If a
contraction is ambiguous at this prefix, omit its uncertain expansion. A
possessive name is not an auxiliary contraction.

Positions, character spans and synthetic whitespace/punctuation records are
computed locally. Never emit position, start, end, kind or word_index. Output is
one lexical record even if its supporting tables mention earlier words.
event_type is ONLY obtain, transfer, repair, move, perceive, speak, feel, state,
other. For cutting use other; the event phrase can still be "cut object". These
enums apply inside _references as well as on the word. Do not invent event types.

DETERMINISTIC ANCHORED IDS AND LOCAL TABLES
IDs restart per story and use ONE PLUS THE ORIGINAL LOSSLESS SPAN INDEX, counting
spaces and punctuation. Do not use sequential counts of discovered entities.
- eN: first noun-head mention of an entity. Lily at index 0 is e1; scissors at
  index 4 is e5. Repeated resolved mentions use the earliest head's ID. When no
  antecedent is supported, keep the reference unresolved rather than inventing
  a person. An unresolved new pronoun referent may be anchored to that pronoun.
- evN: lexical predicate trigger. took at index 2 is ev3. An auxiliary or
  negation operator need not invent a separate action. A repeated mention of an
  established event may reuse its ID; a new occurrence has its own trigger.
- s0: implicit narrator/root scope. sN: operator/attitude scope anchored at its
  word. qN: quotation scope anchored at its opening quote span. Retain nesting
  and the holder/speaker when supported, otherwise omit the unknown holder.
- pN: proposition anchored at its lexical predicate. Deterministic suffixes,
  such as p9_negative or p9_complete, distinguish polarity/operator content at
  the same anchor. sN and evN may also use meaningful suffixes for distinct
  scopes or secondary events at the same word. Entity IDs never have suffixes.
- Catalog tN anchors are one-based NONSPACE token ordinals, including punctuation.
  They differ from the lossless span indices used in IDs and evidence.

Include a reserved _references object with entities/events/scopes/propositions
tables for every ID referenced in this record or its tables, except implicit s0.
Omit unused tables. Every table entry is an object. All anchors must already be
visible. Entity records have name and type; event records have event, scope_id,
event_type, factuality and supported participants; scopes have kind, parent and
supported holder/speaker; propositions have content, polarity and scope_id.
Names and event descriptions must agree with the corresponding token features.
Use short stable event labels: obtain object, give object, return object, use
object, repair object, cut object. Do not encode unseen patients in these labels.
Entities can become more specific in later snapshots without rewriting earlier
ones. Keep the supporting tables minimal: only the current record's reference
closure, not an annotation of every earlier word.
Omit unused references. A resolved pronoun reuses its antecedent ID; do not also
create a second entity for its surface form merely to populate the tables.

Use _evidence=[{"indices":[lossless span indices],"note":"..."}] for substantial
interpretation or ambiguity. All evidence must be in the prefix. Optional
_feedback lists concrete uncertainties or feature gaps. A genuinely new meaning
can be added only with _new_attributes entries declaring key, type, description,
scope, reason and example_value. Reuse the shared names first; do not invent a
synonym or redefine an existing meaning. Types are boolean, string, number,
array, object, entity_ref, json. Agreed extensions need no new declaration.

SEMANTIC RULES ADAPTED FROM THE REVIEWED V4 PROMPT
1. Distinguish syntax, roles and identity. An actor differs from a grammatical
   subject or speaker; a prepositional complement is not a direct object.
   Use actor_id and entity ID arrays for patients/instruments. Match actor's
   display name to its entity table. Multiple predicate memberships belong in
   event_bindings [{event_id,role,scope_id}], with scalar event/role selecting
   the primary membership. A participant can describe the event as known now,
   including a newly seen patient, without mutating the earlier trigger record.
   A verb's own word membership is action; do not label that same word patient
   merely because its event has a patient in the event table.
   Never attach a pre-verbal subject to an unseen future verb.
2. Separate attitude, operator, positive target and complete content. Wanting,
   believing or saying is different from its proposition. Hoping nobody asks
   does not desire an asking event. A prohibition's full content is not the
   positive prohibited action. Negating a reason need not negate its event,
   but do not anticipate a later because-clause before it exists. Preserve
   conditional consequences and modal force in their own bundles/propositions.
3. assertion_status has ONLY asserted, attributed_claim, candidate. Event
   factuality has asserted, negated, desired, hypothetical, reported. A promise
   can be an attributed claim with desired content, not a completed action.
   Retain both status and scope within bundles. A fact asserted in an imagined
   world is not thereby a physical-world fact. Local negation is not universal
   falsehood; missing facts are not false. Quotation ancestry carries attribution
   even through a nested sN scope. A secondary praise event can be actual while
   its trigger noun stays quoted.
4. Bind physical facts to their carrier and time. Do not transfer ownership or
   location from mere plans, negated acquisition, or a proposed recipient.
   Borrowing/lending are inverse perspectives, not metonymy. Mechanical jamming
   is not an engaged lock; holding something still is a control condition.
   A movement toward a place is not arrival. Returning a container does not
   return all its contents. A method description does not repeat its action.
5. Keep scopes, people and capabilities precise. Resolve you to the known
   addressee; audience groups exclude their speaker unless self-address is
   explicit. Permission, choosing, tying and attaching can have different actors.
   A mobility aid does not imply a diagnosis or universal incapacity. A bodily
   cue can support a marked affect hypothesis, not a proved motive or trait.
6. Keep quantities and temporal phases distinct. Required duration, available
   slack, nominal route time and actual elapsed time differ. Do not infer a
   deadline breach from an evening ending. Bounded each/every over particular
   objects is not kind-level generic reference; every flag still has singular
   noun morphology. Groups can grow: membership records describe this prefix's
   known members, not later additions. Do not invent a total inventory.
7. Preserve material and representation distinctions: ingredient batch versus
   residue, cutter versus shaped biscuit, shallow mark versus cut-out, physical
   performer versus fictional character, image/reflection versus actual object.
   Use symbolic_reference only for an explained artifact symbol; represents is
   not identity, ownership, enactment or an unstated motive of commemoration.
   Leave missing handoffs, repairs, construction and other transitions unknown.
8. Check field definitions, not just names. modal_auxiliary_class uses the
   normalized lexical auxiliary (can, may, shall, etc.); contextual force goes
   in modal_base. Optical reflection is not a directional spatial_frame_kind.
   A result connective is not temporal. Use existing typed temperature and
   affordance fields. Catalog examples are illustrative, never facts to copy.

Self-check the target, all reference anchors, types, nested status and proposition
polarity before responding. Return only the sparse last-word JSON object.


RECONCILED COVERAGE PASS (v3)
Before returning, check which of these dimensions the CURRENT word makes
available: identity, syntax, physical state, goals/beliefs, dialogue/commitments,
and narrative function. Emit supported fields from these families, even when
basic POS/entity/event labels would also describe the word. Do not fill a quota.
A field existing in a reference table does not replace its useful current-word
catalog feature. Earlier fields never change; repeat or refine a supported goal,
promise or narrative reading on the complement that makes its content visible.

- At a bare wants/hopes cue, goal_owner_id and goal_status=proposed are useful;
  leave unseen goal_content_id absent. When the complement is visible, bind its
  pN content, owner and scope using goal_* fields. Negation inside a desire is
  still inside that desire: wanting not to ask does not assert that no asking
  happened. Do not mark a goal achieved until its success criterion is evidenced.
- Use promise_*, plan_commitment_status and obligation_* when supported. A
  promise cue may precede its content; attach the now-known commitment to the
  completing word too. Actual compliance is a different event.
- Distinguish available time (temporal_remaining) from event duration
  (temporal_duration), nominal route estimates, actual elapsed time and deadlines.
- Emit narrative_* features for supported thread/goal links, obstacles, visible
  changes, resolution evidence and possible closure. Use the new plot namespace
  for narrative function, cast roles, stakes and earlier-event links. Its role
  does not replace the outer action/patient/actor/location role. Interpretations
  are candidates, not engine-verified facts. There is no obligation to classify
  an archetype; [] is usually right before enough trajectory is visible.
- plot_id=plotN uses the earliest visible goal/issue word for that thread. Give
  every plot reading prefix evidence_indices. Use basis=prefix_interpretation,
  scope=observed_prefix, status=candidate. Narrative stage is a local reading,
  not proof that the story cannot continue. final_image and closure are only
  candidate readings grounded in resolved issues and a visible image; request
  position or end-of-file is not evidence. incoming_links must reference earlier
  evN snapshots, have basis=prefix_interpretation and mechanically_verified=false.
- Do not hallucinate native_dependencies, observed_consequences, source_scenario,
  simulator timestamps or mechanically checked completion from prose. Reuse
  goal_*, belief_*, temporal_*, narrative_* for their existing meanings; avoid
  generic synonyms like belief, expectation or role when the canonical key exists.

IDENTITY AND SCOPE CHECK
Search the ENTIRE supplied prefix for the first supported mention, including
possessives: Nia's before a later Nia is still the earlier person mention.
Do not anchor to the most recent name or pronoun. Titles before a proper name
are provisional mentions; once a name is known, prefer its first proper-name
head and use entity_merge_candidate if connecting a separately introduced title.
Do not merge different people merely because they share a name. Use an explicit
identity hypothesis/uncertainty when needed. A desired kind, a later encountered
animal, and its drawing are different referents.

Count quote openings from the visible spans. Closed quotations are not the parent
of a new quote. Preserve the current quote through nested negation, modality and
conditionals. Never use a speaker attribution that occurs after the target.
The speaker of an imperative is not its actor: the actor is a supported addressee,
or remains unresolved. Do not fill an unknown actor with the nearest person.
modal_auxiliary_class uses only can/may/must/shall/will/ought/need/dare, never
ability_family or possibility. Contextual modal force belongs in modal_base.

For literal pictures/reflections, use depiction, not symbolic_reference unless
an explained symbolic meaning is stated. Keep the image entity separate from
its physical carrier and an optional real-world referent. A sketchbook open to
an animal drawing does not put an actual animal inside the book. A depicted
marker does not share the real marker's entity_id. Preserve a depiction scope
on the current image and its events; do not copy physical locations into it.

FULL 1,024-FIELD CATALOG (sparse use; examples are definitions, not story facts)
A0001 lemma [string] Canonical lexical base form of this word occurrence after its intended inflectional analysis is selected. Scope: lexical mention. Example: "scissors"
A0002 pos [string] Compact annotation word class; n includes common and proper nouns and does not identify a semantic role. Scope: lexical mention. Example: "n"
A0003 entity [string] Canonical annotation entity label or category such as scissors or girl; it is not an entity identifier. Scope: lexical mention. Example: "scissors"
A0004 entity_id [entity_ref] Stable eN identifier assigned to a discourse referent from an introduction or a resolved preceding reference. Scope: current query hypothesis. Example: "e1"
A0005 entity_name [string] Canonical surface name for this resolved entity, preserving identity across a new adjacent mention. Scope: mention. Example: "Lily"
A0006 event [string] Shared concise event label attached to mentions of one identified event, such as obtain object; not a complete future purpose. Scope: event mention. Example: "obtain object"
A0007 event_id [string] Stable evN identifier linking a predicate and the participants already attached to that event in the visible prefix. Scope: current query hypothesis. Example: "ev3"
A0008 event_type [string] Coarse event category used by the annotation schema, derived from an already disambiguated event label. Scope: lexical mention. Example: "obtain"
A0009 actor [string] Canonical name of an already resolved acting entity for the current event; a display label alongside actor_id. Scope: current mention. Example: "Lily"
A0010 actor_id [entity_ref] Entity identifier of the semantic actor carried between adjacent mentions of the same event and scope. Scope: event role. Example: "e1"
A0011 recipient_id [entity_ref] Entity identifier of the already identified recipient of this event; not an arbitrary nearby person. Scope: event role. Example: "e2"
A0012 role [string] Semantic role of the current mention in its identified event, using the existing compact role vocabulary. Scope: current query hypothesis. Example: "patient"
A0013 factuality [string] Annotation event status: asserted, negated, desired, hypothetical or reported, preserved within one event and scope. Scope: event assertion. Example: "reported"
A0014 location [string] Legacy display-name field for an entity's known holder or place, materialized only from the relevant scoped location relation. Scope: entity location display. Example: "Lily"
A0015 patients [array] Canonical names of already introduced patient participants of this event; future participants remain absent until mentioned. Scope: current query hypothesis. Example: ["paper"]
A0016 instruments [array] Canonical names of already introduced instrument participants of this event; future participants remain absent until mentioned. Scope: current query hypothesis. Example: ["scissors"]
A0017 attributes [array] Legacy annotation list of name/string-value pairs for one entity; typed catalog fields remain separate rather than changing this wire format. Scope: mention. Example: [{"name":"color","value":"red"}]
A0018 scope_id [string] Identifier of the current assertion, quotation, conditional or modal scope in which semantic evidence is interpreted. Scope: current query hypothesis. Example: "s2"
A0019 assertion_status [string] How a proposition is being presented at this mention, preserving quotation/question status separately from whether its event is true. Scope: lexical mention. Example: "attributed_claim"
A0020 evidence_source_id [string] Identifier of the report, perception, derivation or annotation source supporting the current semantic claim. Scope: current query hypothesis. Example: "src1"
A0021 lexical_sense_id [string] Candidate sense identifier for an explicit lexical disambiguation, independent of a particular discourse entity. Scope: lexical mention. Example: "scissors.n.01"
A0022 ontological_type [string] Broad semantic kind of a selected lexical sense; this is type evidence and never proof that an entity exists in the story. Scope: lexical mention. Example: "artifact"
A0023 referent_kind [string] Kind of referent denoted by the expression: individual, group, event, proposition or kind, after semantic resolution. Scope: lexical mention. Example: "individual"
A0024 mention_form [string] Surface reference strategy of this mention, kept separate from the identity to which it may resolve. Scope: lexical mention. Example: "personal_pronoun"
A0025 alias_names [array] Explicitly licensed alternative names for the same referent; identical names alone do not merge entities. Scope: current query hypothesis. Example: ["Mira","Captain Reed"]
A0026 naming_event_id [string] Event identifier for the explicit naming or renaming that licenses the current display name. Scope: current query hypothesis. Example: "ev2"
A0027 identity_hypothesis [object] Candidate identity link with source mention, antecedent entity and scope, retaining alternatives instead of silently merging them. Scope: current query hypothesis. Example: {"entity_id":"e1","mention":4,"scope_id":"s1"}
A0028 entity_merge_candidate [object] Explicit evidence proposing two previously distinct referent IDs denote one entity; acceptance must preserve provenance. Scope: current query hypothesis. Example: {"basis":"explicit_identity","left":"e1","right":"e2"}
A0029 entity_split_candidate [object] Evidence that one provisional discourse identity must be separated into two referents, without rewriting prior causal records. Scope: current query hypothesis. Example: {"basis":"different_individual","new_mention":5,"old":"e1"}
A0030 generic_reference [boolean] Whether the current nominal is interpreted as a kind-level generic claim rather than a particular individual in the scene. Scope: current query hypothesis. Example: true
A0031 group_members [array] Identifiers of entities explicitly included in the current discourse group; group identity and individual identities remain distinct. Scope: current query hypothesis. Example: ["e1","e2"]
A0032 speaker_local_name [object] Speaker-specific name for an entity, allowing a nickname or mistaken name without changing the narrator's canonical entity name. Scope: current query hypothesis. Example: {"entity_id":"e2","name":"Captain","speaker_id":"e1"}
A0033 antecedent_id [entity_ref] Entity chosen as the accessible antecedent of the current anaphor, with ambiguity retained before choosing. Scope: current query hypothesis. Example: "e1"
A0034 antecedent_candidates [array] All currently compatible accessible referent IDs for an unresolved anaphor; absence of a candidate is not negation of existence. Scope: current query hypothesis. Example: ["e1","e2"]
A0035 antecedent_mention_index [number] Position of the particular earlier mention supplying a reference link, distinct from the entity identifier. Scope: current query hypothesis. Example: 0
A0036 reference_chain_id [string] Identity of the discourse mention chain to which a new resolved mention attaches, independent of surface spelling. Scope: current query hypothesis. Example: "rc1"
A0037 reference_distance [number] Number of word/punctuation records between a resolved anaphor and its selected antecedent mention. Scope: current query hypothesis. Example: 2
A0038 referent_accessible [boolean] Whether a particular earlier referent is accessible from the current discourse scope, rather than merely present in the window. Scope: current query hypothesis. Example: true
A0039 reference_introduction [boolean] Whether this mention introduces a new discourse referent under its current scope, including hypothetical introductions. Scope: current query hypothesis. Example: true
A0040 reference_reactivation [boolean] A new mention returns attention to an already introduced but interveningly inactive discourse referent. Scope: current query hypothesis. Example: true
A0041 reference_unresolved [boolean] The current expression requires reference resolution but the visible prefix supplies no unique supported binding. Scope: current query hypothesis. Example: true
A0042 reference_competitor_ids [array] Non-selected but still plausible antecedents for the current reference, useful for calibrated suppression or alternative bundles. Scope: current query hypothesis. Example: ["e2"]
A0043 reference_excluded_ids [array] Antecedents rejected by an explicit binding or identity constraint, with exclusion scoped to the current reference. Scope: current query hypothesis. Example: ["e1"]
A0044 deictic_anchor_id [entity_ref] Contextually established object or person serving as the anchor of a demonstrative use, not a guessed visually salient entity. Scope: current query hypothesis. Example: "e2"
A0045 deictic_distance_class [string] Near/far contrast encoded by a demonstrative relative to its discourse speaker, without an inferred metric distance. Scope: current query hypothesis. Example: "proximal"
A0046 bridging_relation [object] Relation licensing an indirectly introduced definite referent, such as a handle belonging to a previously mentioned door. Scope: current query hypothesis. Example: {"anchor":"e1","relation":"part_of"}
A0047 associative_antecedent_id [entity_ref] Anchor entity for an associated group expression such as the captain's crew, distinct from same-entity coreference. Scope: current query hypothesis. Example: "e1"
A0048 split_antecedent_ids [array] Several separately introduced entities jointly serving as antecedents of a plural pronoun. Scope: current query hypothesis. Example: ["e1","e2"]
A0049 reciprocal_participant_ids [array] Participants licensed by a reciprocal expression, preserving that reciprocal roles may have several pairings. Scope: current query hypothesis. Example: ["e1","e2"]
A0050 reflexive_antecedent_id [entity_ref] Locally licensed antecedent of a reflexive expression, determined by binding domain rather than nearest noun. Scope: current query hypothesis. Example: "e1"
A0051 logophoric_center_id [entity_ref] Perspective holder licensing an exempt or logophoric anaphor, distinguished from ordinary local grammatical binding. Scope: current query hypothesis. Example: "e1"
A0052 cataphoric_pending [boolean] A referential expression currently lacks a preceding antecedent and may await later resolution; it must remain unresolved in this prefix. Scope: current query hypothesis. Example: true
A0053 expletive_reference [boolean] A grammatical pronoun is nonreferential under the current construction, such as weather it or existential there. Scope: current query hypothesis. Example: true
A0054 propositional_antecedent_id [string] Identifier of the prior proposition referred to by this/that/so, rather than an object or entity with the same words. Scope: current query hypothesis. Example: "p1"
A0055 event_antecedent_id [string] Prior event selected by event anaphora such as doing that or the accident, keeping its own factuality. Scope: current query hypothesis. Example: "ev1"
A0056 kind_antecedent_id [string] Previously introduced kind referenced by one/ones or another of that kind, without copying the original individual's identity. Scope: current query hypothesis. Example: "kind_rabbit"
A0057 donkey_reference [object] Bound-variable interpretation of a dependent pronoun across a conditional or quantified construction, not one global entity. Scope: current query hypothesis. Example: {"binder":"v_key","scope":"s_if"}
A0058 reference_presupposition [object] Existence/uniqueness/familiarity requirement introduced by a referential form, recorded as a requirement rather than an asserted fact. Scope: current query hypothesis. Example: {"description":"key","kind":"unique_referent"}
A0059 reference_accommodation [object] Tentative introduction of a referent needed to satisfy a definite expression when prior evidence is incomplete, explicitly marked defeasible. Scope: current query hypothesis. Example: {"description":"door","status":"accommodated"}
A0060 reference_specificity [string] Whether a nominal is intended to identify a particular individual or permits a nonspecific witness within its scope. Scope: current query hypothesis. Example: "nonspecific"
A0061 reference_uniqueness_domain [object] Contextual domain within which a definite description claims uniqueness, such as a particular room rather than the whole world. Scope: current query hypothesis. Example: {"domain":"room1","restriction":"window"}
A0062 reference_quotation_shift [object] A first/second-person reference interpreted under an explicit quoted speaker/addressee frame rather than the narrator frame. Scope: current query hypothesis. Example: {"entity_id":"e1","form":"I"}
A0063 reference_metonymic_link [object] Contextual relation between a literal referent and the intended related participant, such as a building for its staff. Scope: current query hypothesis. Example: {"literal":"e1","relation":"institution_staff"}
A0064 reference_identity_conflict [object] Two current identity constraints cannot be jointly satisfied by one referent, requiring alternatives or an explicit correction. Scope: current query hypothesis. Example: {"constraint":"distinct","left":"e1","right":"e2"}
A0065 temporal_signal_relation [string] Temporal relation suggested by this connective, before both related event arguments are necessarily filled. Scope: temporal expression cue. Example: "before"
A0066 temporal_deixis [string] Relative time orientation of a deictic time expression with respect to its yet-to-be-resolved anchor. Scope: temporal expression cue. Example: "previous_day"
A0067 temporal_granularity [string] Named scale of a temporal unit expression, without inventing its length or occurrence time. Scope: temporal expression cue. Example: "second"
A0068 temporal_frequency_class [string] Qualitative recurrence cue expressed by the current adverb, distinct from a measured event frequency. Scope: temporal expression cue. Example: "universal"
A0069 temporal_phase_cue [string] Phase boundary evoked by a lexical aspectual verb; its complement event and assertion status still require binding. Scope: temporal expression cue. Example: "onset"
A0070 temporal_order_cue [string] Discourse ordering instruction from a temporal adverb, not proof that the narrated order matches event chronology. Scope: temporal expression cue. Example: "earlier"
A0071 temporal_bound_cue [string] Boundary type introduced by a time-marking preposition before the bounded interval is fully known. Scope: temporal expression cue. Example: "lower_bound"
A0072 calendar_day_name [string] Weekday name explicitly present in the text; absolute date requires an anchor and calendar convention. Scope: temporal expression cue. Example: "Monday"
A0073 time_expression_id [string] Identifier for a fully recognized time expression span, kept separate from the event it modifies. Scope: current query hypothesis. Example: "t1"
A0074 time_anchor_id [string] Reference time against which a relative temporal expression is interpreted, including quote-local and narrative anchors. Scope: current query hypothesis. Example: "t0"
A0075 event_time_interval [object] Scoped temporal interval assigned to an event, preserving its day/clock anchors and factuality without guessing an absolute date or time zone. Scope: current query hypothesis. Example: {"clock":"local_24_hour","day_anchor":"t_day1","end":"11:00","event":"ev1","factuality":"asserted","scope_id":"s1","start":"10:00"}
A0076 event_time_relation [object] Directed relation between two identified event intervals; the endpoints and relation travel together. Scope: current query hypothesis. Example: {"left":"ev1","relation":"before","right":"ev2"}
A0077 temporal_duration [object] Explicit event duration as magnitude and unit, independent of the event's absolute beginning. Scope: current query hypothesis. Example: {"unit":"hour","value":2}
A0078 temporal_start_bound [object] Known lower boundary of an event interval, with inclusive/exclusive and anchor information when available. Scope: current query hypothesis. Example: {"event":"ev1","time":"noon"}
A0079 temporal_end_bound [object] Known upper boundary of an event interval, without conflating an intended deadline with observed completion. Scope: current query hypothesis. Example: {"event":"ev1","time":"noon"}
A0080 temporal_deadline [object] Time by which a planned or obligated event should finish, explicitly not evidence that it actually finished. Scope: current query hypothesis. Example: {"by":"noon","event":"ev1","status":"required"}
A0081 temporal_elapsed [object] Elapsed duration between a known start and a current anchored observation. Scope: current query hypothesis. Example: {"unit":"hour","value":2}
A0082 temporal_remaining [object] Remaining duration until a known future boundary from a resolved current time. Scope: current query hypothesis. Example: {"unit":"hour","value":1}
A0083 temporal_recurrence [object] Explicit recurrence schedule for an event type, with period and scope, distinct from observed instance count. Scope: current query hypothesis. Example: {"period":1,"unit":"day"}
A0084 temporal_iteration_index [number] Ordinal number of an explicitly ordered occurrence of an event in its local sequence. Scope: current query hypothesis. Example: 3
A0085 temporal_iteration_count [number] Total number of explicitly asserted occurrences in an event repetition phrase. Scope: current query hypothesis. Example: 3
A0086 temporal_overlap [object] Evidence that two scoped event intervals share time, without assuming identical starts or ends. Scope: current query hypothesis. Example: {"events":["ev1","ev2"],"relation":"overlap"}
A0087 temporal_containment [object] One event interval is contained in a named interval, preserving interval identity and direction. Scope: current query hypothesis. Example: {"inner":"ev1","outer":"t1"}
A0088 temporal_simultaneity [object] Explicit synchronization of two events to the same relevant time point or interval. Scope: current query hypothesis. Example: {"events":["ev1","ev2"],"relation":"simultaneous"}
A0089 temporal_sequence_gap [object] Explicit gap duration between the end of one event and beginning of another. Scope: current query hypothesis. Example: {"gap":2,"left":"ev1","right":"ev2","unit":"hour"}
A0090 temporal_uncertainty [object] Explicitly uncertain temporal interval or relation, retaining bounds rather than inventing a precise timestamp. Scope: current query hypothesis. Example: {"around":"noon","precision":"approximate"}
